chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, on the authority of al-Sakuni, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali (peace be upon them all):
That the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) prohibited using four epithets (kunyas): Abu Isa, Abu al-Hakam, Abu Malik, and Abu al-Qasim if the name is Muhammad.

key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ: Peace be upon him and his family

ai.seo_question: What are the four kunyas prohibited for someone named Muhammad in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* highlights the Prophet’s specific prohibition against using 'Abu al-Qasim' for those named Muhammad to preserve the distinctiveness of the Prophet’s kunya, while also cautioning against 'Abu Isa', 'Abu al-Hakam', and 'Abu Malik'. Shia scholars interpret this as a measure to prevent confusion with the Prophet and to avoid attributing divine attributes like 'Master of Judgment' to oneself. The ruling underscores the high status of the Prophet’s names and the etiquette of humility in adopting honorifics.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-117 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (ra) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Muqayrih, on the authority of Al-Sakoony, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (a.s), on the authority of his father (a.s), on the authority of his forefathers (a.s), on the authority of Ali (a.s), “ That the Prophet (sw) prohibited using four epithets; Abu ‘Isa, Abu al-Hakam, Abu Malik, and Abu al-Qasim if the name is Muhammad.’”
